antipatterns: app/Jobs/PushStockAllocations.php:70 a closure ($query = fn () => ...) used as a query factory is a bit clever; two plain queries or ->clone() would read more clearly
tests/Feature/StockSyncTest.php:183-189 the test only checks that middleware() has one entry and that a limiter is registered, a weak structural assertion
app/Console/Commands/DispatchStockSync.php:43 lockForUpdate inside the per-batch transaction is redundant with onOneServer, and it is a no-op on SQLite (harmless)
strengths: Job only sends rows that are still claimed (whereNotNull sync_started_at), so a duplicate SQS delivery or stale job does not re-push synced rows (verified by probe)
Proactive RateLimited('storefront-stock') middleware backed by Redis cache, plus 429 handling with tooManyRequests() and a clamped Retry-After
retryUntil (13 min) is tied to CLAIM_TIMEOUT_MINUTES; failed() releases the claim so the next dispatcher run re-picks the rows
synced_at is captured before the read, so edits made while the request is in flight stay ready; the sync and disable writes share one transaction
Uses toBase() for claim/sync writes so updated_at is not bumped, and comments only the non-obvious why
Modern Laravel 13 idioms: #[Signature]/#[Description], #[Scope], #[Fillable], #[Timeout]/#[Backoff]/#[MaxExceptions], Http::preventStrayRequests, onOneServer + withoutOverlapping

bugs: Job does not require rows to still be claimed (app/Jobs/PushStockAllocations.php:41-44), so a duplicate SQS delivery or late-running stale job re-POSTs rows that were already synced; probe showed 2 HTTP calls for one change, violating 'sent exactly once per change'
No proactive rate limiting: all 50 jobs from a 5,000-row run hit the slow API concurrently and rely only on 429 releases, burning attempts and risking retryUntil expiry
A 200 response with {"missing": null} throws TypeError from in_array (line 66), so a successful push is retried or failed instead of being marked synced
Sync and disable updates (lines 68-72) are not in a transaction, so a crash in between leaves the missing rows claimed until the 15-minute expiry
$sentAt is taken after the read, which leaves a small window where an edit between the read and now() would be lost
antipatterns: app/Console/Commands/DispatchStockSync.php:28-32 claims with an update and then re-reads by exact sync_started_at equality, a fragile claim check that depends on timestamp precision
tests/Feature/Stock/PushStockAllocationsTest.php:44-54 'can run twice' asserts only that synced_at is set, missing the double send
database/migrations/..._create_stock_allocations_table.php no index for the readyToSync query
strengths: Clean chunkById-based dispatcher with a bounded claim per chunk
Tests are well organised into three files and cover the 429 cap, Retry-After, failed() requeue, the in-flight edit, schedule overlap settings and the unique sku
retryUntil tied to CLAIM_TTL_MINUTES, with a docblock explaining why releases make a time bound necessary
toBase() for bookkeeping writes, with a concise scope docblock explaining why
Uses partition() for unknown vs accepted and modern attributes (#[Scope], #[Fillable], queue attributes)

v.rationale: Both suites pass and both implementations follow the same overall design: a readyToSync scope, claims written with toBase(), retryUntil kept inside the 15-minute claim window, failed() releasing the claim, and onOneServer plus withoutOverlapping on the schedule. impl-1 is more correct on the task's focus. Its job only sends rows that are still claimed, so duplicate SQS deliveries do not re-push (confirmed by probe; impl-2 sent twice). It also throttles calls with a RateLimited middleware backed by the shared Redis cache instead of relying on 429 releases alone, sets synced_at before the read, wraps the final writes in a transaction, and handles a null 'missing' safely (impl-2 throws TypeError). impl-2 has more tests in better-organised files, but some are weak, including one that hides the double-send bug, and its claim relies on fragile timestamp equality. impl-1 ranks first.
